children.name: Austrorossia
children.description: Austrorossia — a genus of cephalopods.

children.name: Austrorossia australis
children.description: Austrorossia australis, often called the big bottom bobtail squid, is a species of bobtail squid in the family Sepiolidae. This species lives in sandy and muddy environments from 131 to 665 meters deep, in waters away from South Australia, New South Wales, Victoria, Tasmania, and Queensland.

children.name: Austrorossia bipapillata
children.description: Austrorossia bipapillata, or the big-eyed bobtail squid, is a species of cuttlefish.

children.name: Austrorossia enigmatica
children.description: Austrorossia enigmatica is a species of bobtail squid native to the south-eastern Atlantic Ocean; it occurs off the coast of southern Africa from Namibia to Cape Province, South Africa. It lives at depths from 276 to 400 m.

children.name: Austrorossia mastigophora
children.description: Austrorossia mastigophora is a species of bobtail squid native to western, southern and eastern Africa, from Guinea and Somalia to the Cape of Good Hope. A doubtful record of this species exists from Chile. It lives at depths to approximately 640 m.

children.name: Sepiolina
children.description: Sepiolina — a genus of cephalopods.

children.name: Sepiolina nipponensis
children.description: Sepiolina nipponensis, also known as the Japanese bobtail squid, is a bobtail squid and one of two species in the genus Sepiolina. It is found in the Western Pacific in apparently widely separated populations, the most southerly of which is in the Great Australian Bight in South Australia and Western Australia, and there are populations from the Philippines northwards to Taiwan, Fujian and southern Honshū.

children.name: Nectoteuthis
children.description: Nectoteuthis — a genus of cephalopods.

children.name: Euprymna
children.description: Euprymna — a genus of cephalopods.

children.name: Euprymna albatrossae G.L.Voss, 1962
children.description: Euprymna albatrossae is a species of bobtail squid native to the western Pacific Ocean off the Philippines and Japan.

children.name: Euprymna berryi Sasaki, 1929
children.description: Euprymna berryi, commonly called hummingbird bobtail squid or Berry's bobtail squid among various other vernacular names, is a species of mollusc cephalopod in the family Sepiolidae.

children.name: Euprymna brenneri G.Sanchez, Jolly, A.Reid, Sugimoto, Azama, Marlétaz, Simakov & Rokhsar, 2019
Euprymna bursa
children.description: Euprymna is a genus of bobtail squid comprising a number of species.

children.name: Euprymna hoylei Adam, 1986
children.description: Euprymna hoylei is a species of bobtail squid native to the tropical waters of the Indo-Pacific, specifically the western Pacific Ocean and northwestern Australia.

children.name: Euprymna hyllebergi Nateewathana, 1997
children.description: Euprymna hyllebergi, the Thai bobtail squid is a species of squid belonging to the family Sepiolidae and is native to the eastern Indian Ocean.

children.name: Euprymna morsei
children.description: Euprymna morsei, the Mimika bobtail squid, is a species of Indo-Pacific bobtail squid from the family Sepiolidae.

children.name: Euprymna penares
children.description: Euprymna penares is a species of bobtail squid native to waters of the Indo-Pacific; its exact distribution is unknown. Little is known about the size range of this species.

children.name: Euprymna scolopes S.S.Berry, 1913
children.description: __NOTOC__ Euprymna scolopes, also known as the Hawaiian bobtail squid, is a species of bobtail squid in the family Sepiolidae native to the central Pacific Ocean, where it occurs in shallow coastal waters off the Hawaiian Islands and Midway Island.

children.name: Euprymna stenodactyla
children.description: Euprymna stenodactyla is a species of bobtail squid.

children.name: Euprymna tasmanica
children.description: Euprymna tasmanica, also known as the southern dumpling squid or southern bobtail squid, is a bobtail squid that lives in the shallow temperate coastal waters of southern Australia's continental shelf. It lives for between 5 and 8 months and the adults can grow up to 6 or 7 cm long with a mantle length of 3 to 4 cm. They are found in seagrass beds or areas with soft silty or muddy bottoms from Brisbane on the east coast to Shark Bay on the west, as well as around Tasmania.

children.name: Rondeletiola
children.description: Rondeletiola — a genus of cephalopods.

children.name: Rondeletiola minor
children.description: Rondeletiola minor, also known as the lentil bobtail, is a species of bobtail squid native to the eastern Atlantic Ocean and Mediterranean Sea. Its natural range covers the northwest of Spain, Portugal, and the eastern, central and western Mediterranean Sea to the southeastern Atlantic Benguela Current off Namibia.

children.name: Neorossia
children.description: Neorossia — a genus of cephalopods.

children.name: Neorossia caroli
children.description: Neorossia caroli, the Carol bobtail squid, is a species of bobtail squid belonging to the family Sepiolidae.

children.name: Neorossia leptodons A.Reid, 1992
children.description: Neorossia leptodons is a species of bobtail squid native to the southwestern Pacific Ocean, from New South Wales ( ) to South Australia ( ).

children.name: Inioteuthis
children.description: Inioteuthis — a genus of cephalopods.

children.name: Inioteuthis japonica Verrill, 1881
children.description: Inioteuthis japonica is a species of bobtail squid native to the western Pacific Ocean, specifically the waters off China, Taiwan, and southern Japan.

children.name: Inioteuthis maculosa Goodrich, 1896
children.description: Inioteuthis maculosa is a species of bobtail squid native to the Indo-Pacific.

children.name: Stoloteuthis
children.description: Stoloteuthis — a genus of cephalopods.

children.name: Stoloteuthis leucoptera
children.description: Stoloteuthis leucoptera, also known as the butterfly bobtail squid, is a widespread species of bobtail squid. Its natural range covers the Atlantic Ocean, Mediterranean Sea, and southwestern Indian Ocean. It is distributed from the Gulf of St Lawrence to the Straits of Florida in the western Atlantic and in the Bay of Biscay in the eastern Atlantic.

children.name: Stoloteuthis maoria
children.description: Stoloteuthis maoria is a species of bobtail squid native to the southwestern Pacific Ocean. It occurs in Cook Strait and Chatham Rise off North Island in New Zealand, and has also been recorded from the Nazca and Sala y Gomez submarine ridges in the eastern Pacific.

children.name: Stoloteuthis weberi
children.description: Stoloteuthis weberi is a species of bobtail squid native to the Indo-Pacific waters off central Indonesia.

children.name: Iridoteuthis
children.description: Iridoteuthis — a genus of cephalopods.

children.name: Iridoteuthis iris
children.description: Iridoteuthis iris is a species of bobtail squid native to the northern central Pacific Ocean; it occurs near the Hawaiian Islands off the southeast and northwest Hancock, Colahan, and Kammu seamounts. There exists a doubtful record from the Ceram Sea. Unlike most other bobtail squid, I.

children.name: Sepietta
children.description: Sepietta — a genus of cephalopods.

children.name: Sepietta oweniana
children.description: Sepietta oweniana is a common marine mollusc from the order Sepiida, the cuttlefish.

children.name: Semirossia
children.description: Semirossia — a genus of cephalopods.

children.name: Semirossia patagonica
children.description: Semirossia patagonica is a species of bobtail squid native to the south-western Atlantic Ocean and south-eastern Pacific Ocean; it occurs around the southern part of South America and has been recorded from waters off Chile, Anegada Bay, Tierra del Fuego, Argentina, and the Falkland Islands.

children.name: Semirossia tenera
children.description: Semirossia tenera, also known as the lesser bobtail squid, is a widespread species of bobtail squid native to the northwest Atlantic Ocean. Its natural range covers the eastern coast of North America, from the northern Gulf of Maine to the Gulf of Mexico and the Caribbean Sea. tenera is possibly also present in the southwest Atlantic, specifically off the coasts of Suriname, French Guiana, Brazil, and Uruguay, although the latter records are questionable.

children.name: Sepiola
children.description: Sepiola — a genus of cephalopods.

children.name: Sepiola atlantica d'Orbigny, 1842
children.description: Sepiola atlantica, also known as the Atlantic bobtail, is a species of bobtail squid native to the north-eastern Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea.

children.name: Sepiola rondeletii Leach, 1817
children.description: Sepiola rondeletii, also known as the dwarf bobtail, is a species of bobtail squid native to the northeastern Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea, including the Strait of Sicily, Aegean Sea, Adriatic Sea, Sea of Marmara, and Levantine Sea.

children.name: Sepiola rossiaeformis Pfeffer, 1884
children.description: Sepiola rossiaeformis is a species of bobtail squid native to the Indo-Pacific.

children.name: Sepiola steenstrupiana Levy, 1912
children.description: Sepiola steenstrupiana, also known as Steenstrup's bobtail, is a species of bobtail squid native to the Gulf of Aden in the Red Sea, waters off Somalia, and the Mediterranean Sea, including the central Tyrrhenian Sea, the Adriatic Sea, the Aegean Sea, and the Levantine Sea.

children.name: Rossia
children.description: Rossia — a genus of cephalopods.

children.name: Rossia brachyura A.E.Verrill, 1883
children.description: Rossia brachyura is a species of bobtail squid native to the tropical western Atlantic Ocean, specifically the Greater and Lesser Antilles.

children.name: Rossia bullisi G.L.Voss, 1956
children.description: Rossia bullisi, also known as the Gulf bobtail squid, is a species of bobtail squid native to the tropical western Atlantic Ocean, specifically the northern Gulf of Mexico and Straits of Florida.

children.name: Rossia glaucopis Lovén, 1845
children.description: Rossia glaucopis is a species of bobtail squid native to the south-eastern Pacific Ocean, specifically the waters around Chile.

children.name: Rossia megaptera A.E.Verrill, 1881
children.description: Rossia megaptera, also known as the big-fin bobtail squid, is a species of bobtail squid native to the north-western Atlantic Ocean, specifically Davis Strait, western Greenland, and off New York, in Hudson Canyon.

children.name: Rossia moelleri Steenstrup, 1856
children.description: Rossia moelleri is a species of bobtail squid native to the northern Atlantic Ocean and the Arctic Ocean, eastward to the Laptev Sea and westward to Amundsen Bay.

children.name: Rossia mollicella Sasaki, 1920
children.description: Rossia mollicella is a species of bobtail squid native to the western Pacific Ocean, south from Sendai Bay, Japan.

children.name: Rossia pacifica S.S.Berry, 1911
children.description: Rossia pacifica, also known as the stubby squid, is a species of bobtail squid native to the northern Pacific Ocean.

children.name: Rossia palpebrosa Owen, 1835
children.description: Rossia palpebrosa, also known as the warty bobtail squid, is a species of bobtail squid native to the northern Atlantic Ocean.

children.name: Heteroteuthis
children.description: Heteroteuthis — a genus of cephalopods.

children.name: Heteroteuthis dagamensis G.C.Robson, 1924
children.description: Heteroteuthis dagamensis is a species of bobtail squid native to the south-eastern Atlantic Ocean and south-western Indian Ocean.

children.name: Heteroteuthis dispar
children.description: Heteroteuthis dispar, also known as the odd bobtail, is a small deep water squid found in the North Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea.

children.name: Heteroteuthis hawaiiensis
children.description: Heteroteuthis hawaiiensis is a species of bobtail squid native to the central and western Pacific Ocean. It occurs in waters off Hawaii, Bonin, the Ryukyu Islands, Indonesia, and the Great Australian Bight. hawaiiensis may also be present in Banc Combe in the southwestern Pacific at depths of 795 to 820 m.

children.name: Choneteuthis
children.description: Choneteuthis — a genus of cephalopods.

children.name: Choneteuthis tongaensis Lu & Boucher-Rodoni, 2006
children.description: Choneteuthis tongaensis is a species of bobtail squid native to the waters around the Tonga Islands in the southern Pacific Ocean.

children.name: Amphorateuthis
children.description: Amphorateuthis — a genus of cephalopods.

children.name: Eumandya
children.description: Eumandya — a genus of cephalopods.

children.name: Eumandya phenax
children.description: Eumandya phenax is a species of bobtail squid native to the waters of the Indo-Pacific, off the Philippines and possibly in the East China Sea. The depth range of this species is unknown. It was originally collected by nightlight.
